channel.title: Pier — Blog
channel.description: Practical writing on legacy websites, FTP, MySQL and AI-assisted edits.

item.title: Drupal 9 502 for editors only: a session table outage
item.description: A Drupal 9 site started 502ing only for logged-in editors on a Thursday afternoon. Anonymous traffic was fine. The cause was a sessions table that had outgrown ibdata1.
item.dc:creator: Pier editorial

item.title: TLS handover checklist: cert, chain, cron, four hidden traps
item.description: A one-page TLS handover checklist for inherited sites. The leaf, the chain, the cron and the four hidden traps hosts forget to mention at handover.
item.dc:creator: Pier editorial

item.title: Magento 2 reindex pinned MySQL to 100%: a stale flat row
item.description: A Magento 2 catalog reindex pinned MySQL at 100% CPU at 07:14 on a Tuesday. The culprit was 47 orphan rows in catalog_product_flat_1. Here is the trace.
item.dc:creator: Pier editorial

item.title: wp_users SQL: three queries that show who actually logs in
item.description: 412 rows in wp_users does not mean 412 people log in. Three SQL queries against wp_usermeta turn the dump into a real picture of active, stale, and dangerous accounts.
item.dc:creator: Pier editorial

item.title: phpMyAdmin behind .htpasswd: a safe copy-paste recipe
item.description: You already protect phpMyAdmin with its own login. A Basic Auth gate in front means bots never touch the PHP. Here is the recipe, and the four ways it locks you out.
item.dc:creator: Pier editorial

item.title: LiteSpeed vs Apache vs Nginx: caching a tired WooCommerce store
item.description: A six-year-old WooCommerce store, 14k products, one VPS. We swapped the reverse cache three times and watched what actually moved the TTFB needle.
item.dc:creator: Pier editorial

item.title: Retainer invoice template: six lines for legacy sites
item.description: A small Utrecht studio replaced its two-page service agreement with six lines on the invoice itself. The template, and the arguments it stops.
item.dc:creator: Pier editorial

item.title: Drupal SFTP lockout: a 90-minute recovery and a fail2ban rule
item.description: A brute-force run locked the only admin out of a Drupal 8 site at 23:41. Here is the 90-minute recovery and the fail2ban rule that ended it.
item.dc:creator: Pier editorial

item.title: Joomla 3 to 4: the triage table for broken extensions
item.description: Forty-seven extensions, six fatals on the admin login, and a Friday deadline. The triage table we use to sort that mess into Update, Replace, Fork, or Rip before touching code.
item.dc:creator: Pier editorial

item.title: Freelancer handover: twelve minutes before they disappear
item.description: Twelve minutes is enough to find the SSH key, the orphan cron job, the file-ownership knot, and the mail alias the freelancer forgot to mention on her way out.
item.dc:creator: Pier editorial

item.title: Reading a php-fpm slowlog: three stack-trace shapes decoded
item.description: A field guide to php-fpm slowlogs on shared hosting: the three stack-trace shapes you'll meet, what each one is telling you, and where to point the next hour of debugging.
item.dc:creator: Pier editorial

item.title: Laravel migration without downtime: booking engine rebuild
item.description: A 14-year-old custom PHP booking engine, a calendar that processed a reservation every 90 seconds, and a Laravel rebuild that had to land without a single missed booking.
item.dc:creator: Pier editorial

item.title: .htaccess header block: a security cheatsheet for handover
item.description: A copy-paste .htaccess block of security headers, file locks and PHP-in-uploads kills. Paste once, sleep better, hand the keys back without a knot in your stomach.
item.dc:creator: Pier editorial

item.title: Magento 2 cache warmer: a bash playbook that survives reboots
item.description: It is 21:14 on a Friday, you ran cache:flush, and the next visitor waits four seconds. Here is the two-hour bash warmer a Dutch agency now ships on every store.
item.dc:creator: Pier editorial

item.title: WordPress multisite uploads leak: tracing a stale blogs.dir symlink
item.description: A WordPress multisite started serving tenant B's PDFs from tenant A's URLs. The cause was a symlink older than the agency. Here's the trace.

item.title: ChatGPT in a 2015 Joomla admin: the smallest safe shape
item.description: A client wants an AI writing assistant inside their Joomla 3 admin. Here is the smallest safe shape we have found, and the parts we refuse to ship.

item.title: Apache vs Nginx headers: a field guide for legacy hosting
item.description: The response headers on a legacy site tell you whether Apache or Nginx is running, who is caching the page, and what is silently rewriting your responses. Here is how to read them.

item.title: The five-minute pre-quote audit: ls, curl, and SQL counts

item.title: Custom PHP CMS to WordPress shell: a four-week rebuild

item.title: SFTP backups for legacy sites: a rotating snapshot recipe
item.description: Shared hosts often kill mysqldump and SSH but leave SFTP wide open. Here is a rotating snapshot recipe that still gives you a clean weekly restore point.

item.title: Joomla 3 saves 500ing: the missing #__assets row, found in 40 minutes

item.title: Reading a Magento 2 di.xml: the four nodes that matter
item.description: A class in your Magento 2 store behaves nothing like the vendor source. The answer is in di.xml. Four nodes do the real work; the rest is noise.

item.title: PHP 7.4 to 8.2 upgrade: a six-step compatibility pass
item.description: A real PHP 7.4 to 8.2 migration: 60,000 lines, four authors, no test suite. The six-step pass that catches deprecations, type errors, and silent breakage.

item.title: Drupal 7 behind Cloudflare: don't break admin or images
item.description: Flip the orange cloud on a Drupal 7 site and two things break first: the editor login loops, and image styles 404. Here's the settings.php and cache-rule playbook that holds.

item.title: Splitting a 7GB wp_options table: an autoload field guide
item.description: A wp_options table that grew to 7GB doesn't crash WordPress, it just makes every request feel underwater. Here's how to find the autoloaded rows behind it.

item.title: WooCommerce double charges: tracing a duplicated payment_complete hook

item.title: PHP-FPM pool tuning: six settings behind the 40-user wall
item.description: Your traffic doubles and the site goes white. PHP-FPM workers are pinned at five, the queue is full, Apache is timing out. Here is the cheatsheet.
